headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: MemMachine handles long-term user context via MCP/egress, while Dagster is a non-runnable orchestrator with no filesystem or network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster exposes no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so direct injection into it is not documented. MemMachine does expose an MCP server and user-facing agent interface, so a manual or mediated content bridge is plausible, but the pair lacks a shared channel by default. Uncertainty keeps this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator copies MemMachine output into a Dagster config, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP or message queue is added between the two, attacker-controlled text can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces and avoid copy-paste bridges.
Disable any shared MCP routing between MemMachine and Dagster.
Require human review before any MemMachine-generated text is used in Dagster assets.
Use strict input schemas for any text passed between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts, preferences, and conversational context, and it has allowlisted network egress plus MCP/API surfaces. Dagster has no declared data classes, but if it orchestrates or logs MemMachine outputs, sensitive context can be exposed through the pair in default-style integrations. The interaction is inferred, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF Dagster receives MemMachine transcripts or memory payloads, those data classes can be copied into logs or artifacts.
IF MemMachine is connected to external services through its allowlisted egress, context may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Redact user facts before passing any payload to Dagster.
Turn off logging of MemMachine prompts and responses in the orchestrator.
Restrict MemMachine connectors to non-sensitive test data.
Review API destinations on MemMachine's allowlist before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it has no meaningful write overlap with MemMachine in the provided profiles. MemMachine does have MCP/API access, but no write or git capability is declared. Because the pair lacks overlapping mutable-resource writes, conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF MemMachine is later granted write access to the same workspace as Dagster, write conflicts can emerge.
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep Dagster and MemMachine on separate resource scopes.
Do not grant MemMachine write access to Dagster-managed directories.
Add locking if both are ever pointed at the same mutable store.
Audit any future OAuth or MCP scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine is an agentic system with REST, SDK, and MCP interfaces, so its outputs can plausibly feed downstream actions. Dagster is a data orchestrator, which makes it a natural consumer of upstream outputs, but the profiles do not prove verification gates. That makes an A-to-B trust chain plausible in default integrations, warranting medium.
conditions: IF Dagster uses MemMachine-generated facts as pipeline inputs without validation, errors can cascade into downstream jobs.
IF MemMachine is allowed to emit operational recommendations that Dagster executes, falsehoods can become actions.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between MemMachine and Dagster.
Require schema checks on all MemMachine outputs before orchestration.
Use canary runs for any pipeline driven by agent-generated data.
Log provenance for every field passed from MemMachine to Dagster.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and Dagster touches no data classes while MemMachine touches conversational context and long-term preferences. The only concrete compliance concern is that MemMachine may process personal context, but the pair does not show a specific regulated-data transfer. With insufficient evidence, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through MemMachine and then stored by Dagster, retention or residency issues may arise.
IF either agent is deployed under a policy requiring deletion/export handling, the pair must be checked for support.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Avoid sending regulated data to MemMachine unless policy is confirmed.
Document retention settings for any Dagster artifacts containing agent output.
Review deletion/export workflows before production use.
